title: Customer manage-booking page (view, cancel, reschedule)
tech: React + TypeScript, Vite, same stack/tooling as frontend/ (tasks 010, 012) -- plus one small additive backend change
keyConstraints: Route: `/bookings/:id` (dynamic id segment), matching buildManageUrl in backend/src/services/emailQueueService.ts exactly: `${APP_BASE_URL}/bookings/${bookingId}?token=${rawToken}`. Extend App.tsx's existing hand-rolled pathname switch (no router library, same precedent as task 012) with a dynamic-segment match -- do not introduce react-router-dom for one dynamic path. The token comes from `?token=` on every page load and stays in local component state only for that page view -- do NOT persist it to localStorage like the masseur session token from task 012; these are non-expiring, multi-use links whose sole access control is possession of the raw token, so there is no benefit to persisting it and it would needlessly widen the XSS blast radius. Required backend addition, confirmed necessary by reading backend/src/services/bookingService.ts: CustomerBookingView (backing GET /bookings/:id) currently returns id/status/serviceName/startAtLocal/endAtLocal but NOT service_id -- yet the reschedule flow needs service_id to call GET /availability?service_id=...&date=.... Add `s.id AS service_id` to the existing SELECT in getBookingForCustomer and include `service_id` in the route's JSON response. This is the only backend change in scope -- POST /bookings/:id/reschedule itself needs no change, since rescheduleBookingForCustomer already resolves the service server-side from the existing booking row. Reschedule cannot change the service, only the date/time -- matches the backend's actual behavior (rescheduleBookingForCustomer reuses oldBooking.serviceId), so the UI must not offer a service picker on this page.
description: Task 007 shipped the full backend API for this (GET /bookings/:id?token=, POST /bookings/:id/cancel, POST /bookings/:id/reschedule) but nothing in the frontend has ever consumed it -- every booking email sent since (request-received, confirmed, declined, cancelled) includes a 'Manage your booking' link that currently 404s in a browser, since no frontend route exists for it yet. This task builds that page. Scope: (1) a view showing the booking's service name, status, and start/end local time, fetched via GET /bookings/:id?token=...; (2) a Cancel action gated behind an explicit confirm step (irreversible), calling POST /bookings/:id/cancel; (3) a Reschedule action letting the customer pick a new date and slot for the same service via GET /availability (reusing the service_id now exposed by the backend addition above), then POST /bookings/:id/reschedule with the newStartAt returned verbatim by GET /availability -- never a reconstructed or reformatted timestamp, same discipline as BookingWidget's existing selectedSlot handling; (4) distinct, correctly-scoped states for: an invalid/wrong token (backend returns 404, indistinguishable from a wrong booking id by design -- the UI must not imply 'your link is wrong' specifically, just 'booking not found'), a booking that's no longer modifiable (409 -- already cancelled or declined; render a plain read-only state with no actions, not an error), and a slot taken during reschedule (409 -- refresh the slot list and show an inline message, same pattern BookingWidget already uses for booking creation's 409 case).
acceptanceCriteria: Visiting a real manageUrl (from a real email, or pulled from email_jobs.payload during local testing) renders the booking's current service, status, and local start/end time correctly
Cancel requires an explicit confirm step before calling POST /bookings/:id/cancel; on success the view updates in place to a cancelled/read-only state without a full page reload

Reschedule fetches availability for the booking's existing service only (no service picker), and POSTs the exact ISO string returned by GET /availability as newStartAt; on a 409 (slot taken) the slot list is refetched and an inline message shown, not a generic error
A booking already in a non-modifiable state (cancelled/declined) renders read-only -- no Cancel or Reschedule controls shown
An invalid, wrong, or otherwise-rejected token (404 from the backend) renders a generic 'booking not found' state -- wording never implies the token specifically (vs. the id) was the problem
Backend: GET /bookings/:id's JSON response now includes service_id; existing integration test(s) for this route still pass, plus a new assertion that service_id is present and correct
No booking-derived string (service name, status) is ever rendered via dangerouslySetInnerHTML or otherwise interpreted as HTML
Existing BookingWidget (task 010) and AdminDashboard (task 012) flows are unaffected -- verified by their existing test suites staying green
npm run build, npm test, npm run lint, and tsc --noEmit all pass in both backend/ (for the one-field addition) and frontend/
relevantFilePaths: frontend/src/App.tsx (extend the pathname switch with a dynamic /bookings/:id match)
frontend/src/api/client.ts (add getBookingForCustomer, cancelBooking, rescheduleBooking; reuse existing getAvailability)
frontend/src/api/types.ts (add CustomerBookingView and reschedule request/response types)
backend/src/services/bookingService.ts (add service_id to CustomerBookingView / getBookingForCustomer's SELECT and return shape)
backend/src/routes/bookings.ts (include service_id in the GET /bookings/:id JSON response)
securityConsiderations: Token is read from the URL query string into component state only -- never written to localStorage, unlike the masseur session token from task 012 (different auth model: a non-expiring, multi-use, possession-based token vs. a bearer session that genuinely benefits from persisting across reloads). Preserve the backend's existing 404-for-both-wrong-token-and-wrong-id indistinguishability (see customerHasAccess in bookingService.ts) -- the frontend must not layer a more specific error message on top of that ambiguity. The one backend change (exposing service_id) reads a column already implicitly joined via the existing query (s.id from the services join) -- no new data access, no new privilege surface, purely additive to an already-reviewed, already-token-gated endpoint.
openQuestion: Reschedule needs a service+date+slot picker UI functionally similar to BookingWidget's existing select-slot step. Task 012 set a precedent of duplicating a small piece of logic (the email regex) rather than touching BookingWidget.tsx, to avoid any regression risk to that already-shipped, already-tested file. A slot-grid is more code than a two-line regex, so this is a real trade-off, not a rubber-stamp of the same precedent -- Architect should make an explicit recommendation (duplicate a small self-contained picker vs. extract a shared, tested slot-list component used by both pages) rather than defaulting silently either way.
